The **Debugger** shows what the framework did for each request — route, user, timing, every SQL statement, what was logged and what failed — in the spirit of the Yii debug toolbar. It is a page in the Desk, a chip in the Desk top bar and a JSON API that scripts and AI agents can query.

| Panel | Shows |
|-------|-------|
| **Requests** | The latest requests of this tenant: method, URL, status, user, duration, query count. Open one for its full detail |
| **Database** | Every query with its duration and (redacted) bindings; **slow** queries (≥ 100 ms) and **repeated** statements (≥ 5 per request — a likely N+1) are flagged |
| **Logs** | `console.*` output, per request and process-wide |
| **Errors** | Errors with their stack, linked to the request that raised them |
| **Status** | Versions, mode, build, memory, the tenant's database engine and install state, and apps with a **pending update** |
| **Tests** | Run the test suite (development only) |
| **API access** | Tokens for the JSON API |

The **top-bar chip** lists your own latest requests and lights up when new errors appear. Every response carries an `X-Loopar-Debug: <id>` header pointing to its entry. The page updates live over the realtime socket.
"}},{"node":"debugger-config","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Turning It On","key":"debugger-config","id":"debugger-config","name":"debugger-config","value":"## Turning It On

The Debugger is **on by default in development and off in production**. Override it in `config/core.json`:

```json
{ "debug": true }
```

(or `LOOPAR_DEBUG=1`). It is read at boot — restart the core to apply.

### What it keeps, and what it never keeps

- Storage is **in memory**, one bounded bucket per tenant (the latest 300 requests, 1,500 log lines, 300 errors…). Everything is lost on restart — it is a development tool, not an audit log.
- A tenant only ever reads **its own** bucket. Output of the core itself and requests without a tenant go to a bucket no tenant can read.
- Anything that looks like a credential is **redacted before it is stored**: SQL bindings of sensitive columns, request parameters and headers with sensitive names, and values shaped like password hashes, JWTs or debug tokens.

Access in the Desk follows permissions: the Administrator, or roles granted the `Debugger` actions.
"}},{"node":"debugger-api","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"JSON API","key":"debugger-api","id":"debugger-api","name":"debugger-api","value":"## JSON API

Every panel is also an endpoint: `/api/Debugger/<action>`. From the Desk session they work like any action; from outside (a script, a CI job, an AI coding agent) use a **debug token**:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ldbg_<id>_<secret>" \
  "https://dev.example.com/api/Debugger/latest?status=500"
```

| Action | Scope | Returns |
|--------|-------|---------|
| `manifest` | read | Description of the API itself |
| `status` | read | `{ info }` — framework and tenant status |
| `requests` · `request?id=` · `latest` | read | Recorded requests (filterable) |
| `queries` · `logs` · `errors` | read | Across requests |
| `testFiles` · `testRun?id=` · `testRuns` | read | Test files and runs |
| `runTests` · `cancelTests` | run | Start (`suite`, `files`, `namePattern`, `wait` seconds up to 600) or cancel a run |

Payloads are wrapped under a named key (`request`, `run`, `rows`…) because `status`, `code` and `message` belong to the response envelope.

### Tokens

Create them in **API access**: a label, a scope (**read**, or **run** to also start tests) and a lifetime (1–365 days, or 0 = never expires). The token is shown **once**; only its hash is stored, with its last use time and IP. Disable or revoke it there. A debug token only opens the Debugger API — it never stands in for a user anywhere else.
"}},{"node":"debugger-tests","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Testing","key":"debugger-tests","id":"debugger-tests","name":"debugger-tests","value":"## Testing

Loopar's suite is built on `node:test` — no extra dependencies.

```bash
yarn test                                                   # everything
yarn test:unit                                              # pure modules, no tenant
node --test --test-force-exit test/integration/permissions.test.js   # one file
```

| Folder | Contains |
|--------|----------|
| `test/unit/` | Pure modules: helpers, validators, the query translator on in-memory SQLite, backup crypto and retention… |
| `test/integration/` | Tests against a **real tenant** |

### Integration tests

`bootTestTenant()` creates a throwaway tenant (`sites/__loopar_test_<pid>__`, SQLite), installs the `loopar` app through its real installer and removes it in `teardown()`. Code that touches the tenant runs inside `t.run()`:

```javascript
import { test, before, after } from "node:test";
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { loopar } from "loopar";
import { bootTestTenant } from "../support/tenant.js";

let t;
before(async () => { t = await bootTestTenant(); });
after(async () => { await t?.teardown(); });

test("the core app is installed", () => t.run(async () => {
  assert.equal(await loopar.db.count("App", { name: "loopar" }), 1);
}));
```

### Three ways to run them

| Where | How |
|-------|-----|
| Terminal | `yarn test` |
| TUI | `T` opens the Tests tab: live status per file, failures with their assertion diff; `a` all, `u` unit, `i` integration, `f` re-run failed, `x` stop |
| Desk | Debugger → **Tests** (development mode only), or `POST /api/Debugger/runTests?suite=unit&wait=120` with a `run` token |

All three run the suite in a **child process** (never inside the core) and clean up any test tenant a run leaves behind. Only one run executes at a time per core.
